Ekan sadvipra bahudha vadanti | Truth is one, the wise call it by many names
Two of the most quoted lines in Indian philosophy come from one hymn of the Rigveda, 1.164, the great riddle hymn: two birds on one tree, one eating the sweet fig, the other only watching; and truth is one, the wise call it by many names. The two birds return in the Mundaka and Shvetashvatara Upanishads; this is where they began.
